events.text:
### Priority list
1. `#recommendations` — dominates the rendered page (326,112px² of the 399,977px² main area) and is the actual JS-injected content (raw HTML only has empty placeholder divs), so getting the delayed swap-in behavior and card markup right is the main fidelity risk.
2. `.product-card` (×3, repeated fragment) — each one is sizeable (108,704px²) and together they make up nearly all of `#recommendations`; need to confirm via red-twine that all three share the same structural pattern before treating them as one component.
3. `h1` "Recommended for you" — second-largest single element (46,768px²) and the only static text on the page, so it must be transcribed verbatim.

events.text: Outlines match exactly (identical positions/sizes). Now let's confirm pixel-for-pixel with odiff.

input.command: cd /var/folders/gb/m6478s0n5mx9wqlz8t_c03800000gn/T/gumshoe-agent-run-XJBIwn && npx odiff-bin original.png clone-round1.png diff-round1.png --parsable-stdout; echo "exit: $?"

events.text: odiff reports 0 pixel difference (exit code 0, exact match) — this confirms a pixel-perfect clone. Let's verify visually for completeness.

Visually identical, confirming the odiff result. The clone is complete and pixel-perfect on the first pass, so no further iteration rounds were needed. ## Summary **What the page actually was:** a minimal "lazy-loaded recommendations widget" fixture — raw HTML ships three empty `
` elements inside `#recommendations`, and inline JS swaps them for real `.product-card` markup (image + name + price) after a 150ms `setTimeout`, simulating an async API response. There is no CSS anywhere in the source — every visual property (h1 at 32px/700 weight, block-level margins on `div`/`p`, inline `span`) comes purely from the browser's default UA stylesheet. **Key decisions:** - **Componentization:** red-twine confirmed the three placeholder divs (and, by extension, the three product-cards they become) are one repeated structural pattern sharing the `.placeholder`/`.product-card` shape — treated as a single card component repeated 3×, not three bespoke blocks. - **JS-gated content confirmed directly:** reading the raw HTML source made the JS-injection explicit (the code comment even says so), and crow-nester's rendered outline showed the post-timeout `.product-card` state — no need to spend a slowcure call proving what was already unambiguous from source + outline. - **No Tailwind/design tokens introduced:** windtailor against `body` showed zero custom CSS anywhere — just plain UA defaults (the only "token" it minted was `text-32` for the h1's default 32px size). Since there's no real design system to extract, I did **not** bolt on a Tailwind CDN — doing so would have pulled in Tailwind's preflight reset, zeroing out the exact default margins/font-sizes that determine this page's actual layout, and would have hurt fidelity rather than helped it. The clone is a faithful 1:1 reproduction of the original markup, CSS-free, same inline script and 150ms timeout behavior. - **Images left as-is:** the `` references are relative paths with no real host behind this local fixture; per scope, I kept them exactly as authored rather than inventing a placeholder or rehosting. - **Nothing flagged as unrecreatable** — this page had no canvas, video, or cross-origin iframe content requiring a fidelity caveat. **Screenshot comparison:** one round was sufficient. `original.png` vs `clone-round1.png` (both 1280×900, post-JS state) came back from odiff at **0 changed pixels / 0.00% difference** (exit code 0 — exact match), and side-by-side visual inspection confirmed the two renders are indistinguishable. All screenshots (`original.png`, `clone-round1.png`, `diff-round1.png`) are saved in the run directory alongside `clone.html`.
